predictions.title: AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears 15GW threshold by H2 2026
predictions.body: By H2 2026 the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clears a 15GW cumulative threshold, anchored by the third-consecutive-week sovereign-cloud signing cadence and the AI-accelerator IPO comparable set that Wednesday's tape has now firmed into a single readable supply-and-demand picture. The Wednesday catalysts trace a tightening run-up to the T-minus-one-day Thursday May 21 Alphabet analyst day. A Wednesday HPCwire AIwire note reports the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book advancing to near 10.7GW with a fresh weekday sovereign-cloud commitment, the third new commitment of the business week and the highest weekly cadence the book has carried since the program opened. A Wednesday Datacenter Dynamics wire reports the Tenstorrent Galaxy-rack first-half capacity-fulfillment curve crossing the 70-percent threshold for the first time, at roughly 71 percent of the 280-rack target on a cumulative count of 198 racks deployed, with the third European sovereign-cloud increment of the week going to Outscale France plus Atlante Cloud Italy and the third Asia-Pacific increment splitting between Yotta Labs India and CDS Japan. The capital-markets backdrop hardens on the same Wednesday tape: Cerebras CBRS holds the Friday $198.60 close as its reference anchor with the five-desk analyst spread carrying inside a roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging to about 39 percent of float on the analyst-day eve, and a Wednesday 247 Wall St note reporting the Mag-7 preview cohort clearing the 90-percent threshold on Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability — the first time the cohort consensus has cleared that line — with the cohort treating Wednesday's pre-print Cerebras session as a coincident input. The Wednesday AIwire note further reports Tenstorrent's SEC Corp Fin first-round comment-letter response at its 13-business-day mark inside the staff-review interval with the second-round letter expected late Thursday or Friday, the early-August public-filing target holding, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster steady at six — giving equity analysts a fresh three-name AI-accelerator IPO comparable set against which the AMD commitment-book trajectory and the Tenstorrent capacity-fulfillment curve land as the two readable demand-side anchors. That fast-signing run is now historical: the book peaked at roughly 11.1GW on Friday May 22 as the first week's cadence topped out, and across the weeks since it has sat at that ~11.1GW landmark with no fresh sovereign-cloud signings printing — the three-per-business-week pace did not continue, and the most recent datapoint is a July Advancing AI event-calendar preview rather than a new commitment. The realistic path to 15GW therefore runs not off a compounding weekly cadence but off a slower, lumpier signing trajectory measured from the settled ~11.1GW base — likely re-accelerated by a discrete catalyst such as the July Advancing AI event where MI400 / MI455X availability is detailed — that still has room to add the remaining ~3.9GW inside the back half of 2026. The most likely landing is the AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book clearing 15GW cumulative inside H2 2026, with the sovereign-cloud cohort supplying the marginal-signing share above the ~11.1GW landmark, the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 leaning on its ~80-percent capacity-fulfillment curve as the revenue-traction anchor when it goes public, and the Mag-7 fiscal-Q3 AI Services breakouts pricing the AMD book as a demand-side comparable. Bear case is that the signing pause extends and the next sovereign-cloud increments keep slipping their execution windows, leaving the book short of 15GW at year-end; the 15GW threshold itself still holds as the H2 2026 outcome, but only off a slower trajectory than the May run-up implied, not the three-per-week arithmetic the program briefly carried.

reasoning.because: Commitment book settled at ~11.1GW on May 22 and held flat since; the fast weekly cadence stalled.
reasoning.given: The ~11.1GW landmark is a stable base; Tenstorrent fulfillment ~80%; July Advancing AI the catalyst.
reasoning.so_that: The book still clears 15GW cumulative inside H2 2026, off a slower lumpier trajectory, not a weekly cadence.
reasoning.landing: By H2 2026; sovereign-cloud cohort drives marginal signings above ~11.1GW.
reasoning.plain_language: AMD's AI-server order book stalled at about 11GW, but it should still reach 15GW of orders by late 2026, just more slowly.

predictions.summary: The AMD Helios plus MI450 commitment book settled at roughly 11.1GW on May 22 and has held there since, the fast three-per-week sovereign-cloud signing cadence now dormant. Off that base, a slower lumpier trajectory — likely re-catalyzed by July's Advancing AI event — still clears 15GW in H2 2026.
